title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ يتقدم الجموع في مسيرة نصرة القدس العالمية
title_en: The Sheikh Leads the Crowds in the Global March in Support of Jerusalem
body_ar: ألقي فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن بن الددو- أمس الجمعة 6/6/2014- كلمة في مقدمة الجموع الحاشدة التي لبت دعوة الشيخ للمشاركة في المسيرة العالمية لنصرة القدس (التي نظمها الرباط الوطني لنصرة الشعب الفلسطيني) وسط العاصمة نواكشوط. وتحدث الشيخ حفظه الله في كلمته عن فضل القدس مبينا أن الله جعل الولاية عليها لرسولنا صلى الله عليه وسلم ،حين أم الانبياء جميعا فيها ؛ فكان ذلك إيذانا بأنها أمانة في يد أمته . وقد تسلم عمر ابن الخطاب رضي الله عنه مفاتيحها وهي اليوم تنادي في الامة روح صلاح الدين في وقت يمعن فيه اليهود في الفساد بها ، ويحفرون الانفاق تحت المسجد الاقصى مما يهدد المسجد ويعرضه للتصدع والهدم. وختم الشيخ بالدعاء موجها الدعوة إلى الأمة حكاما ومحكومين ليقوموا بما أوجب الله عليهم من نصرة المجاهدين في فلسطين ، والمرابطين بالمسجد الأقصى ،مبينا أن باب النصرة يشمل كل أطياف المجتمع وتخصصاته فللحكام أدوارهم وللتجار أدوارهم، وللطلاب دور حاضر ومتميز، وللكتاب والإعلاميين دور مؤثر . وقد جرت المسيرة في جو من الهدوء والسكينة طالب الشيخ بالمحافظة عليه أثناء الانصراف.
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan ibn al-Dedew delivered an address yesterday, Friday 6/6/2014, at the head of the massed crowds who had answered the Sheikh's call to take part in the Global March in Support of Jerusalem — organised by the National League for the Support of the Palestinian People — in the centre of the capital, Nouakchott.

In his address the Sheikh (may God preserve him) spoke of the merit of Jerusalem, explaining that God gave authority over it to our Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) when he led all the prophets in prayer there, and that this was a declaration that it is a trust in the hands of his community. Umar ibn al-Khattab (may God be pleased with him) received its keys; and today it calls out within the community for the spirit of Saladin, at a time when the Jews persist in working corruption in it and are digging the tunnels beneath the Aqsa Mosque, which threatens the mosque and exposes it to cracking and collapse.

The Sheikh closed with supplication, directing a call to the community, rulers and ruled alike, to carry out what God has made obligatory upon them by way of support for those engaged in jihad in Palestine and those stationed at the Aqsa Mosque; explaining that the door of support takes in every part of society and every field within it — the rulers have their parts, the merchants have theirs, the students have a present and distinguished part, and writers and media people have an influential part.

The march took place in an atmosphere of calm and quiet, which the Sheikh asked be maintained as people dispersed.

flags.arabic: في وقت يمعن فيه اليهود في الفساد بها
flags.context: the Sheikh's characterisation of the present situation in Jerusalem, as the site reports it
options: the Jews persist in working corruption in it
the Jews are going to great lengths in corruption there
flags.note: EDITORIAL. The report has the Sheikh speaking of 'the Jews' as a collective actor in Jerusalem. Translated exactly as the Arabic has it — not narrowed to 'the Israelis' or 'the occupation', which would be an improvement on the source and a change to what is attributed to him, and not sharpened either. Read in English, outside the political register of a 2014 Nouakchott rally, the sentence is liable to be quoted as a statement about Jews as such. Whether and how to publish is for Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office, never for the translator. Note also that these are the site's words reporting him, not a quotation.

flags.arabic: نصرة المجاهدين في فلسطين، والمرابطين بالمسجد الأقصى
flags.context: the call the Sheikh addressed to the community
options: support for those engaged in jihad in Palestine and those stationed at the Aqsa Mosque
support for the mujahidin in Palestine and those holding the frontier at the Aqsa Mosque
support for the fighters in Palestine and those keeping vigil at the Aqsa Mosque
flags.note: EDITORIAL and terminological. مجاهدون and مرابطون both carry a military sense in classical usage, and مرابطون is also the ordinary word in Palestinian usage for those who keep presence at the mosque without fighting. The English keeps both terms visible rather than resolving them into either 'fighters' or 'worshippers'. Neither is in the project glossary; both are candidates for addition, since they recur across the corpus and the choice has consequences.

flags.arabic: أن الله جعل الولاية عليها لرسولنا صلى الله عليه وسلم، حين أم الانبياء جميعا فيها
flags.context: the argument from the night journey
options: God gave authority over it to our Messenger
God made guardianship of it belong to our Messenger
God assigned its custodianship to our Messenger
flags.note: ولاية spans authority, guardianship and custodianship, and the choice affects how strong a claim the sentence makes. Rendered 'authority' as the least specific. No text is cited for the inference and none has been supplied.

translator_notes: A news report of a rally address. Nothing is directly quoted; the whole account is in the site's words, and the English must not be cited as the Sheikh's own wording.
The record contains scattered missing hamzas (الانبياء, الامة, الانفاق, الاقصى); these are not individually flagged.
The dating is unusually clear here: the address was Friday 6 June 2014 and the CMS stamp is Saturday 7 June, so the upload followed the event by a day. That is not true of the range generally.
